name: Brí Léith

attributes.attribute: a famous fairy mound at the center of Ireland
the palace of Midir, greatest of fairy kings
named for the heroine Brí, possibly another name for Étain

sources: Gwynn, Edward. The Metrical Dindshenchas. Part II. Vol. IX. Royal Irish Academy, Todd Lecture Series. Dublin: Hodges, Figgis, and Co. Ltd., 1906. Pp. 3, 299-301.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Brí Léith is a hill of Ireland that works as a gate of the Otherworld. It is the modern Ardagh Hill, three miles from a Longford town. The fairy king Midir makes Brí Léith his home. The hero Angus Óg lives there too in older accounts. In the Wooing of Étain, the men of Eochaid Airem plan to tear down the hill as they search for the lost woman. People keep the Lugh festival on the hill until recent times. So the high place holds both a royal tale and a live custom.

okr.objective: Describe Brí Léith, the famous central Irish fairy mound.
key_results: Brí Léith was a famous fairy mound in the center of Ireland.
It was the palace of the fairy king Midir.
Most of its tales concern Étain.
Its name may be another name for Étain.
